headline: High: AutoGen can write and execute code while dbt-core can reach a data warehouse, creating default-path risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen ingests tool calls and code execution per agent role, with files and stdin/stdout surfaces; dbt-core can interact with a data warehouse. If AutoGen consumes dbt-generated text or artifacts as instructions, a shared workspace or copied outputs can become an injection bridge. The pairwise pathway is plausible, but not directly documented here.
conditions: IF AutoGen reads dbt-produced files or stdout as instructions
IF both agents share a writable workspace without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of dbt outputs as prompts
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent artifacts
Review any copied text before reuse

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and has broad network egress plus filesystem access; dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can call the warehouse API. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive warehouse data can be exposed through AutoGen's broader egress path. The profiles do not prove a shared principal, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents run under the same OS account or shared workspace
IF warehouse outputs are copied into AutoGen prompts or files
mitigations: Restrict AutoGen network egress to approved endpoints
Keep warehouse artifacts out of AutoGen context

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem, execute shell commands, and spawn subprocesses; dbt-core can write to a warehouse via its API surface. These overlapping mutation capabilities can conflict on shared artifacts or shared downstream resources even without git writes. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so concurrent writes are a realistic default risk.
conditions: IF both agents target the same working directory
IF dbt runs against the same mutable warehouse objects AutoGen also edits indirectly

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code and tool outputs that dbt-core may consume as warehouse-facing inputs or artifacts. Because dbt-core is a data-engineering tool, treating upstream outputs as authoritative can turn a mistaken AutoGen result into incorrect warehouse actions or broken models. No verification step is documented in either profile, so the blast radius is potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes AutoGen-produced SQL, configs, or manifests without review
IF AutoGen is allowed to emit action-ready instructions
mitigations: Require human review before dbt execution
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline
Block direct execution of agent-authored warehouse changes

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model provider API keys and application data, while dbt-core touches data warehouse data. If warehouse data includes regulated records and AutoGen sends context to third-party model providers, retention or residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR controls, so the safest supported judgment is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into AutoGen prompts or files
IF model-provider logging/retention differs from warehouse retention
mitigations: Use a provider with suitable contractual terms
